title: إِدْغَام كَبِير مُتَمَاثِلَيْن
titleEn: Idghām Kabīr Mutamāthilān in one word
description:
Idghām refers to merging of two letters either wholly or partially. The first letter is  called the mudgham and the second the mudgham fῑh. Idgham kabīr occurs when both the mudgham and mudgham fῑh are mutaḥarrik. Idghām occurs between two letters due to the relationship between said letters. These relationships span across 4 options:
 • Mithlān: Both letters are identical, e.g. ب & ب. • Mutajānisān: Both letters share the same makhraj and have similar sifaat, e.g. ت and د. • Mutaqārībān: Both letters are approximate in makhraj and sifaat e.g. ق and ك. • Mutabāʿidān: Both letters are entirely different, no idgham will occur in this case. This section talks about the rules when idghām kabīr mithlān occurs in a single word.

shatibiyyahReference.notes: Note from al-Shaṭibīyyah Idghām kabīr only occurs for Imam Sūsī .

no_idgham_kabir_mithlain_with_exception.title: No idghām kabīr mithlān with one notable exception
no_idgham_kabir_mithlain_with_exception.description: When two identical mutaḥarrik letters  come together in one word there is no merging (idghām) between them.
exceptions: The notable exception are the words مَنَاسِكَكُمْ (2:200) and سَلَكَكُمْ  (74:42) where there will be a merging of the ك
